title: Energy debuts new Genesis Mission, quantum computing initiatives
key_facts: The Energy Department announced new Genesis Mission funding and a quantum effort at the White House AI Science Summit on Thursday 8 Oct 2026.
A Genesis Mission Graduate Fellowship Pilot, with up to $100 million in total funding, supports PhD students working across AI and science.
Energy named 67 early-career scientists for $96 million, and 12 phase II Genesis Mission projects received $159 million, bringing phase II projects to 14.
Energy released "Quantum Genesis Priority Applications", eight key scientific problems to guide development of the world's first fault-tolerant, scientifically relevant quantum computer.
The Quantum Genesis initiative began in June to deploy such a computer for scientific research by 2028.
A Quantum Genesis Q Competition launched last month offers up to $215 million to US companies proposing quantum computers with at least 100 logical qubits.
quote_evidence: Energy also announced on Thursday the release of Quantum Genesis Priority Applications, which it said are "a set of eight key scientific utility problems" to help guide U.S. development of the world's first fault-tolerant, scientifically relevant quantum computer.
The effort builds on the department's launch of the Quantum Genesis initiative in June to deploy such an advanced computer for scientific research by 2028.
why_it_matters_hint: The US is setting concrete science targets for a usable quantum computer by 2028.
notes: Nextgov reports official DOE announcements. The Register (item C15-12) calls the 2028 goal near-certain to fail given the funding; that is its opinion, not used here.
